title: Midweek ops wireframe check-in (routing/auth/quotas)
content:
Date: 2026-10-11
Attendees: Maya, Jordan, Sofia, Liam, Anika (brief drop-ins: Ravi, Tasha)
Format: 20' sync + walk-the-board wireframe (light on slides, heavy on actions)

Goal for this check-in: triage routing/auth/quotas items that are blocking the mid-sprint deploy and outline short experiments for the weekend capacity window. Treat this as an ops wireframe (quick sketches + owners) rather than a formal RFC review.

Summary bullets (TL;DR):
- Routing fanout change (shard-to-pool affinity) looks safe in staging; p95 latency down ~11% with steady throughput, but KV-cache misses rose ~4%.
- Auth token refresh race still shows intermittent 401 spikes during bursty traffic from a single customer — root cause narrowed to duplicate refresh requests racing on token cache eviction.
- Quotas: new per-customer burst quota is in canary; we observed one fallthrough where fallback routing was not applied due to stale quota metadata.
- Immediate actions: implement short-term token-refresh debounce, add TTL bump on quota metadata writes, and run end-to-end fallthrough simulation Friday 03:00–05:00 UTC.

Observations / metrics called out
- Production snapshot (10/11 08:00–12:00 UTC): aggregate QPS steady at 4.1k, 99p token latency 430ms (baseline 480ms), p95 120ms (baseline 135ms). Serving cost per 1M tokens trending +2% vs last week after the model-variant fallback experiment.
- Staging perf for routing fanout change: p95 down 11%, p99 down 6%. However KV cache hit rate dropped from 92.3% to 88.7% on similar replay. This suggests affinity reduces cross-pool locality benefits for prefix cache.

Routing notes
- Jordan: routed the affinity patch into staging, exercised with traffic replay + synthetic K=64 short prompts. No functional regressions. Observed reduced inter-node RPCs but more local cache misses.
- Proposal: add small local prefix-cache prefetch on shard warm-up to offset misses. Sketch: on first request after new affinity assignment, prefetch last N prefixes (N=3) from global cache into local cache.
- Risk: increases per-shard memory footprint and prefetch adds background load. Mitigation: rate-limit prefetch and only enable for shards > 50% utilization.

Auth notes
- Sofia: confirmed token-refresh race exists for clients that send concurrent requests after token TTL expiry. Two threads call refresh, one succeeds, other sees 401 until cache write propagates.
- Short-term patch: add a server-side debounce (singleflight) keyed by (customer_id, refresh_token_hash) so only one refresh inflight. Rollout plan: toggleable feature flag, enable in canary pool Monday.
- Longer-term: revisit client SDK patterns (documented in SDK issues) and add idempotent refresh APIs. Open question: do we maintain singleflight in front-of-house or push responsibility to token service?

Quota system notes
- Liam: Canary of per-customer burst quotas showed expected throttles, but one case where quota metadata was updated (billing plan change) and the quota-router held stale copy for ~90s. When burst exceeded new quota, router failed to fallback to emergency tier because it consulted local stale metadata and treated customer as unlimited.
- Immediate fix: bump metadata TTL to 15s and add reactive invalidation on billing update events. Done as a config in canary.
- Test plan: run a scripted scenario that changes billing tier mid-flight and verify fallback behavior across 1000 parallel requests. Target window Friday 03:00–05:00 UTC in staging followed by limited prod run Saturday small-window.

Incidents / near misses
- Incident: 2026-10-09 21:12 UTC — increased 401s for customer "AcmeMaps" during a traffic spike. Root cause traced to token-refresh races. No data loss; degraded UX for ~7 minutes. Postmortem in progress (linked).
- Near miss: routing fanout experiment would have caused cold-start amplification for small shards if affinity mapping had been different — caught by synthetic replay.

Action items (owners, quick deadlines)
- Jordan: implement local prefix prefetch prototype and run perf replay by 2026-10-14 (owner: Jordan).
- Sofia: land server-side singleflight debounce (feature-flagged) and deploy to canary Monday 2026-10-13; monitor 401s and latency.
- Liam: increase quota metadata TTL and add reactive invalidation hooks; prepare fallthrough simulation script by 2026-10-13.
- Maya: schedule Friday fallthrough simulation 03:00–05:00 UTC, get SRE oncall standby, and coordinate traffic generator parameters.
- Anika: write short SDK note for client-side best practices around refresh; create an issue to track idempotent refresh API (due 2026-10-18).
- Ravi: add Sentry trace links and example spans to incident notes for postmortem.

Open questions / parking lot
- Prefetch sizing: N=3 is a guess. Need replay experiments to choose N that gives hit-rate improvements > cost.
- Placement of singleflight: front-of-house vs token-service — latency, ownership, and retries differ. We should workshop tradeoffs with auth-service owners.
- Quota fallthrough semantics: how aggressive should automatic fallback be vs explicit per-customer policy? Product input required (cc: @ProductQuota).

Notes for product/security
- Product: the aggressive fallback for quotas surfaced ambiguity in desired UX when a customer is mid-request during plan change. Recommend a short decision doc: when to silently fallback vs return a controlled error.
- Security: token debounce is a mechanism-level change; security review requested. Sofia to add the security checklist link to the PR.

Next steps / cadence
- Quick sync Monday 2026-10-13 09:00 UTC to confirm canary results for singleflight.
- Friday 2026-10-15 03:00–05:00 UTC: fallthrough simulation (staging). After successful run, limited prod test Saturday morning.
- Next full midweek wireframe: 2026-10-18 (same time).

Appendix (commands / test snippets)
- Routing replay command (Jordan): ./tools/replay --trace=affinity-candidate --qps=1500 --duration=10m --seed=stable-2026-10-09
- Quota-change script (Liam): ./sim/quota-change --customer=canary-17 --from=standard --to=burst-blocker --parallel=1000 --sleep=2s
- Token-refresh repro (Sofia): ./auth/test-refresh --concurrency=50 --token-ttl=1s --observe=401

Misc scratch notes (todo in doc)
- Investigate a small TTL-boost for prefix-cache on shard assignment events.
- Check if model-variant fallback cost change correlates with a specific customer heavy usage pattern.
- Remind engineering rotation to include an ops-readout in the oncall handover.

End of notes.

-- Maya
wireframe log: quick, messy, actionable.
